title: Photo transfer onto air-dry clay
subtitle: Transferring a printed image onto a sealed air-dry clay tile
excerpt: A printed image can be transferred onto a sealed air-dry clay surface using a gel medium carrier. The paper backing is rubbed away once the medium dries, leaving the ink layer bonded to the clay. Works with laser or laser-equivalent prints; inkjet prints require a sealing step. No kiln is required.
sourceNotes: Gel-medium transfer technique is a widely documented craft method.

glossaryTerms.definition: A thick acrylic paste that acts as an adhesive carrier for ink transfers; available in matte and gloss finishes

content.text: transfer works by coating the printed side of an image with acrylic gel, pressing it face-down onto a sealed clay tile, then soaking and rubbing the paper away after drying. The ink bonds to the gel and remains on the tile surface. Note that the transferred image is always a mirror of the original, so text must be printed in reverse.

materials.name: Bone-dry air-dry clay tile, sealed with two coats of PVA
Laser-printed image (black and white or colour)

content.text: Print the image in reverse (mirror it in any image editor before printing). Laser prints or photocopies give the clearest transfers. Trim the image to the tile size.
Apply a generous even coat of gel medium to the sealed tile surface using the mop brush. Work quickly as gel begins to dry within 2 minutes.
Lay the image face-down onto the wet gel and press firmly from the centre outward to remove air bubbles. Allow to dry fully for 8 to 12 hours.
Dampen the sponge with water and wet the paper surface gently. Allow the water to soak in for 30 seconds.

Rub the paper in gentle circular strokes with the damp sponge. The paper fibres will begin to ball up and can be rolled away, revealing the ink layer beneath. Work slowly to avoid tearing the ink layer.
Repeat dampening and rubbing until all white paper fibre is removed. Allow to dry between passes to see where residue remains.
Apply two coats of water-based varnish over the transferred image to seal and protect it.

items.problem: Image is very faint or patchy after paper removal
items.cause: The gel coat was too thin or the paper was rubbed before it was fully dry
items.fix: Always wait at least 8 hours before wetting the paper. Apply a thicker gel coat next time. After removal, lightly go over the image area with a thin acrylic wash of similar tones to fill missing patches

items.problem: White paper haze remains over the image even after multiple passes
items.cause: Paper fibres are still present as a thin film
items.fix: Re-dampen, wait 1 minute, then rub more firmly. A slightly damp fingertip is often more effective than a sponge for the final fine paper residue
